about: Château Kirwan takes its name from Mark Kirwan, the heir of a Galway merchant family who settled in Bordeaux in the mid-1700s and renamed the old Domaine de Lassalle after himself. In 1855 it was ranked at the top of the Médoc’s Third Growths, and that same year the botanist Camille Godard, creator of Bordeaux’s Parc Bordelais, restored the château and laid out its gardens. Since 1926 it has belonged to the Schÿler family, Bordeaux wine merchants since 1739, now in its eighth generation.

The 37 hectares of vines lie on a rise of gravel and clay in Cantenac, within the Margaux appellation: Cabernet on sun-warmed gravel, Merlot on clay. In 2015, the driest year in Margaux since 2005, the grapes were picked by hand into small crates between September 18 and October 9, moved by gravity, and fermented in 37 tulip-shaped concrete vats, with alcoholic and malolactic fermentation running together over 18 to 25 days of maceration. The wine then ages in French oak barrels.

The estate describes deep color, dark fruit with black pepper, cinnamon and vanilla, and a fresh palate of velvety tannins with notes of cocoa and coffee before a long finish. Wine Enthusiast gave it 96 points and an Editors’ Choice, while Wine Spectator called it balanced, charming and sure to age gracefully. Kirwan’s Margaux style favors perfume and finesse over sheer weight, and the warm 2015 vintage adds a layer of ripe generosity.
facts: 50% Cabernet Sauvignon, 35% Merlot, 10% Cabernet Franc, 5% Petit Verdot
Concrete tulip vats; simultaneous alcoholic and malolactic fermentation; 18–25 days’ maceration
18–20 months in French oak, about 40% new (estate’s usual regime)
